toegepas.voor: kon 'n nuweling begin boer en het die gemeenskap sterk gebly
toegepas.na: kon 'n nuweling begin boer, en het die gemeenskap sterk gebly
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb (a nuweling kon begin boer / die gemeenskap het sterk gebly); reviewer should confirm the comma does not seem to detach the second clause from the shared 'Omdat'.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS 2017 comma before 'en' joining two main clauses that each have their own subject and verb ('n nuweling kon begin boer / het die gemeenskap sterk gebly).
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma is required by AWS 2017; the inverted 'het die gemeenskap' still ties the second clause to the fronted 'Omdat', so the meaning does not move and no protected wording is touched.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kon so 'n nuweling kalwers vir 'n jaar of twee leen
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kon vir 'n jaar of twee kalwers aan so 'n nuweling leen
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Leen' can mean lend or borrow; 'aan' makes it unambiguous that the community member lends to the newcomer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original double-object 'iemand iemand iets leen' already means lend, not borrow (community member to newcomer); the reordering places 'n jaar of twee' directly before 'kalwers', which a Grade 5 reader can misread as 'one or two calves'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Matches the past tense of the main clause and of the next sentence ('gehad het').
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Afrikaans has no sequence-of-tenses rule, so 'het gesorg dat dit goed gaan' is natural and correct; changing the tense is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'soveel' is the more standard written form than 'so baie' in this construction.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'so baie hande' is natural plain Afrikaans and deliberately echoes the lesson title 'Baie hande maak ligte werk', so 'soveel' is a lateral move that loses the echo.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Dié' is the more natural written form when pointing back to help just described; 'daardie' reads slightly distant and spoken.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Daardie hulp' is natural, plain Afrikaans that a Grade 5 reader follows easily, so swapping it for 'Dié' is a lateral move.
